newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says arrests nine "subversive" youths.
newsitem.headline: Burma says arrests nine "subversive" youths.

text.p: Burma's military government have arrested nine "subversive" youths for distributing leaflets in an attempt to disrupt stability of the state, official media reported on Sunday.

"Action was taken against nine subversive youngsters who were engaged in spreading false and fabricated news among the public with intent to disrupt stability of the nation and community peace and tranquility," state-run newspapers reported.
Three of the youths -- Kyin Thein, Thant Zin and Ngwe Soe -- had allegedly distributed leaflets designed to cause panic and create misleading impressions of the government, the media said.
They were accused of distributing the information at weekend rallies outside Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi's house on University Avenue, it said.
They were also accused of collaborating with six others in distributing the leaflets in other townships.
The youths have not yet been officially charged. The reports did not say when the youths had been arrested.
"Action will be taken according to the law against the nine subversive youths," the newspapers said, without elaborating.
More than 262 members of the National League for Democracy were arrested in a broad crackdown on pro-democracy politicians in May.
Military rulers have since passed a law prohibiting anyone from distributing information seen disruptive to the government.
According to the law, passed in June, violators could be jailed for up to 20 years.
